_comment: A/B replay over identical perception traces. Deltas between
policies are valid; absolute rates are not, because a trace
is sampled at a fixed cadence while the live sampler hashes
every decoded frame. Event and baseline frames are scored
apart: a baseline frame is supposed to be empty.
Each event is scored ONLY against the consequence it actually claims,
and only where that consequence is derivable from the evidence.
TAUTOLOGICAL rows fire by construction and are never credited;
UNTESTABLE rows carry no rate. A frame with no perceptual match was
never put to the test and is counted apart rather than passed.
The reference is an earlier RAW-TRACE frame that resembles this one
— never another retained frame, which would make the baseline move
with the policy under test and stop the rates being comparable.
person_left's claim depends on the departure rule: ON_EXPIRY keeps
the frame after the person is gone and predicts a LOWER count;
LAST_CONFIRMED keeps their final sighting and predicts a NON-EMPTY
frame. Scoring the second with the first's contract reports a
collapse that belongs entirely to the auditor.

person_entered.claim: the person count is higher than in the frame it resembles

person_left.claim: the person count is lower than in the frame it resembles

person_count_changed.claim: the person count differs from the frame it resembles

occlusion_changed.claim: some person's overlap-or-edge state differs; the count need not

region_transition.claim: the multiset of occupied grid cells differs

bbox_changed.claim: a matched box differs in IoU or area beyond threshold

person_moved.claim: a matched box centre has moved at least move_fraction of its diagonal

scene_changed.claim: the perceptual hash differs — true by construction of the trigger

periodic_heartbeat.claim: time has passed — true by construction of the trigger

manual_review.claim: a person wanted it; no observable consequence exists
